findings.title: Test cleanup uses wrong alias literal, causing NPE and test pollution
findings.body: In multiple places (lines 303, 381, 425), the cleanup registration uses `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")` instead of the actual alias variable. The literal string "alias" does not correspond to any created identity provider, so `get("alias")` returns null and calling `.remove()` on it will throw a NullPointerException during cleanup. Moreover, the actual created IDPs will not be removed, leading to cross-test contamination and potentially making other tests fail. This affects both `testCacheIDPByOrg` and `testCacheIDPForLogin`.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException in remove() when alias does not exist
findings.body: In `remove(String alias)`, `storedIdp` is assigned from `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` which may return null if the alias does not exist. If `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, the code calls `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` which dereferences `storedIdp.getInternalId()` and `storedIdp.getAlias()`, causing a NullPointerException. While this path is unlikely in normal flows (the caller usually confirms existence), the method is part of the public storage provider API and should handle null gracefully. The previous code also had this issue, but the refactoring makes it more explicit and still unresolved.
